answer: Agents secure entry by performing 1,000 unique data-repair tasks, a cost honest agents pay once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A verifier monitors each agent for a hollow internal state; if a task log fails to bridge across distinct memory registers during audit, the system flags the result as fraudulent. When an agent reaches a nadir of performance, the verifier triggers an identity burn for detected redundancy. This mechanism assumes individual execution paths cannot be replayed.
